boundaries: The raw Telegram export is local-only and is not a canonical Atlas artifact.
The diagram is an observed artifact, not a universal protocol schema.
Sourced means faithfully attributed; it does not mean independently true.
The Chipnet transaction proves transaction shape and committed bytes, not their private semantics.
PoolActionFv1 backend-neutral semantics are frozen, but deployment configuration and every cryptographic instantiation remain unselected.
Planned vectors, schemas, controls, and projections are not measurements or complete-transaction evidence.
No Atlas Architecture, Module, Claim, Hypothesis, Evidence, or Decision is created by this lane.
No represented option is qualified, product-ready, audited, or recommended for mainnet.
snapshot.objective: Design and qualify a Circle-FRI-based fixed-ticket Bitcoin Cash deposit/withdrawal pool with unilateral spends, one user action per transaction, and no user batching.

postQuantum.claimPolicy: Do not claim the complete system is post-quantum while current BCH or any transaction component retains an unqualified classical dependency.
postQuantum.goal: PQ-oriented proof and private spend path
postQuantum.guardrail: Prefer mature hash-based or otherwise defensible PQ-oriented components, but do not weaken classical security, transaction binding, privacy, availability, standardness, or implementation assurance merely to remove an assumption.
postQuantum.requiredReview: component-by-component assumption inventory covering proof soundness and zero knowledge, hashes, commitments, nullifiers, note authorization, wallet storage and recovery, transaction authorization, and the BCH settlement boundary

soundness.fallbackRule: Select the strongest concretely derived parameter set at or above 100 bits that fits; never lower security silently or optimize an isolated proof component instead of the complete transaction.
soundness.fallbackTrigger: A concretely derived 128-bit configuration cannot fit in one complete 100,000-byte standard BCH transaction after measured protocol, verifier, and encoding optimization.

requires: explicit fixed-denomination, ticket-count, conservation, uniqueness, membership, and transaction-binding relations
strict schema and cross-artifact validation with no fabricated evidence
current-BCH embodiment and standard-transaction reality gates
Circle FRI artifacts with measured soundness, zero knowledge, bytes, VM cost, and adversarial evidence
complete optimized 128-bit deposit and withdrawal transactions before any fallback authorization
trust, liveness, availability, privacy-leakage, and reconstructability review

proofBackendDecision.implementationScope: A direct custom PoolActionFv1 AIR, proof protocol, prover, encoding, and BCH verifier; no generic VM or external prover stack is selected as a dependency.
proofBackendDecision.priorArtPolicy: Stwo and other implementations are evidence and comparison sources only, not protocol authorities or implementation bases.
required: field, extension tower, and circle-domain selection derived from BCH verifier cost
concrete witness masking and zero-knowledge leakage analysis designed with the protocol
explicit Circle-FRI soundness parameters and derivation
BCH-oriented transcript and Merkle hash selection
canonical field encoding, extension arithmetic, and proof parsing
one complete standard BCH transaction per action
under-60-second withdrawal proving on the pinned desktop

scopeDecision.relation: Transparent fixed-ticket deposit followed by one unilateral withdrawal to ordinary BCH.
required: one user action and one action proof per transaction
full on-chain proof and conservation enforcement
no required coordinator or private service

expected.ruleset: May 2026 Upgrade 12 plus May 2025 VM limits
